title: Coupling Break Map

canonical_node.axiom: Coupling breaks when a system has parts, motion, labels, or surface similarity but lacks the load-bearing relation that makes the parts mutually implicating.
definitions: Coupling invariant: the relation that binds parts such that they are mutually implicating.
Distinctness: parts must not collapse into one role.
Dynamics: the system must preserve dynamic relation, not static flattening.
Role profile: the correct three functions must be present, not just three parts.
Source/profile preservation: labels must correspond to preserved structure and source backing.
Entanglement: binding structure beyond mere contact or activation.
Closed-system self-source: a system attempting to power or ground itself from inside itself.
derivation: A system with parts, motion, labels, or surface similarity may still lack the load-bearing relation that makes parts mutually implicating.

The break points are named: no coupling invariant, no distinctness, no dynamics, wrong role profile, relabeling without source/profile preservation, coupling without entanglement, closed-system self-source.
The claim is not 'three things good' but 'three irreducible, correctly profiled, mutually coupled roles pass; malformed three-part systems fail.'

The Maxwell/Trinity gate discriminates: quaternion/full triadic relation passes; vector-only/Heaviside fails coupling invariant; modalism fails distinctness; static single-field fails dynamics; arbitrary three-part system fails role profile; relabeled roles fail source/profile preservation.

The secular triad (quantum substrate + physical laws + decoherence) must be run through the same coupling gate; likely failure is lack of unified mutually implicating act and failure of source/profile/voluntary-coupling gates.
canonical_node.action: Run any candidate triadic system through the coupling gate: check coupling invariant, distinctness, dynamics, role profile, source/profile preservation, and entanglement. Reject malformed triads.
boundary: Does not claim that all three-part systems are valid.
Does not assert that coupling alone is sufficient for the Fall pattern.
Does not claim that secular triads are automatically invalid; they must be tested.
Does not provide a formal proof in this document; it maps break points and gates.
test: Check if the candidate preserves the coupling invariant (e.g., quaternion product vs vector-only).
Check if distinct roles are preserved (e.g., modalism fails).
Check if dynamic relation is preserved (e.g., static single-field fails).
Check if role profile is correct (e.g., arbitrary three-part system fails).
Check if source/profile preservation holds (e.g., relabeled roles fail).
Check if entanglement is present beyond coupling (e.g., coupling without entanglement is not Fall).

classification.recommended_atom_action: preserve as a mapping document; do not treat as proof

May be read as asserting that the secular triad fails without testing.
May be read as claiming that quaternion structure is the only valid coupling invariant without full formal proof.
kill_conditions: If the Lean anchors are not actually present or do not support the stated break points.
If the coupling gate is not formally defined or testable.
If the document is used to claim proof of theological claims without additional evidence.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the coupling gate as a Lean theorem: for any triadic system, if it passes coupling invariant, distinctness, dynamics, role profile, source/profile preservation, and entanglement, then it is valid; otherwise invalid.

plain_summary: This document maps the specific ways in which a triadic system can fail to be a valid coupling: missing invariant, collapsed roles, static structure, wrong role profile, relabeling, coupling without entanglement, and closed self-source. It provides a gate for testing candidates, including secular ones, but does not itself provide formal proof.
